options.D: Create an IAM policy that allows ec2 and rds:* permissions. Attach the policy to a new IAM role. Use the IAM policy simulator to confirm that the policy allows the AWS API calls that are necessary to build the stack. Modify the security engineer's IAM permissions to be able to pass the new role to CloudFormation.

explanations.A: Correct. IAM Access Analyzer policy generation produces a fine-grained least-privilege policy based on observed activity. Attaching it to a dedicated new IAM role and allowing the security engineer only to pass that role to CloudFormation enforces both least privilege and separation of duties between the engineer's account and CloudFormation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Granting ec2 and rds:* permissions is overly broad and violates least privilege, and the option does not generate a precise policy from actual activity. This does not meet the requirements.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Letting the security engineer run the CloudFormation script directly with the generated permissions breaks the required separation of duties between the engineer's IAM account and CloudFormation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ec2 and rds:* permissions are too broad and violate least privilege. Although the IAM policy simulator can validate API calls, it does not produce a least-privilege policy the way IAM Access Analyzer policy generation does.

question: A company that uses AWS Organizations is migrating workloads to AWS. The company's application team determines that the workloads will use Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon S3 buckets, Amazon DynamoDB tables, and Application Load Balancers. For each resource type, the company mandates that deployments must comply with the following requirements: • All EC2 instances must be launched from approved AWS accounts. • All DynamoDB tables must be provisioned with a standardized naming convention. • All infrastructure that is provisioned in any accounts in the organization must be deployed by AWS CloudFormation templates. Which combination of steps should the application team take to meet these requirements? Choose two.)

options.A: Create CloudFormation templates in an administrator AWS account. Share the stack sets with an application AWS account. Restrict the template to be used specifically by the application AWS account.
options.B: Create CloudFormation templates in an application AWS account. Share the output with an administrator AWS account ta review compliant resources. Restrict output to only the administrator AWS account.
options.C: Use permissions boundaries to prevent the application AWS account from provisioning specific resources unless conditions for the internal compliance requirements are met.
options.D: Use SCPs to prevent the application AWS account from provisioning specific resources unless conditions for the internal compliance requirements are met.
options.E: Activate AWS Config managed rules for each service in the application AWS account.

explanations.A: Correct. Creating CloudFormation templates centrally in an administrator account and sharing them as stack sets ensures all infrastructure is deployed through standardized, approved CloudFormation templates, meeting the requirement that all infrastructure be deployed by CloudFormation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Creating templates in the application account and sharing only the output for review does not guarantee that all resources are deployed through CloudFormation, nor does it enforce the organization-level compliance requirements.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Permissions boundaries limit the maximum permissions of IAM users and roles; they are not the mechanism to enforce account-level provisioning controls such as approved accounts or standardized naming conventions across the organization.
explanations.D: Correct. Service control policies are a core AWS Organizations feature that can restrict member account actions with conditions, enforcing requirements such as launching EC2 instances only from approved accounts and applying a standardized DynamoDB naming convention. This meets the requirement.
explanations.E: Incorrect. AWS Config managed rules can monitor and report on resource compliance after the fact, but they cannot prevent non-compliant resources from being created or enforce the mandatory deployment requirements, so they do not meet the requirement.

question: A company has a batch-processing system that uses Amazon S3, Amazon EC2, and AWS Key Management Service AWS KMS .The system uses two AWS accounts: Account A and Account B.Account A hosts an S3 bucket that stores the objects that will be processed. The S3 bucket also stores the results of theprocessing. All the S3 bucket objects are encrypted by a KMS key that is managed in Account A. Account B hosts a VPC that has a fleet of EC2 instances that access the S3 bucket in Account A by using statements in the bucket policy. The VPC was created with DNS hostnames enabled and DNS resolution enabled. A security engineer needs to update the design of the system without changing any of the system's code. No AWS API calls from the batch-processing EC2 instances can travel over the internet. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? Choose two.)

options.A: In the Account B VPC, create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. For the gateway VPC endpoint, create a resource policy that allows the s3 GetObject, s3 ListBucket, s3 PutObject, and s3 PutObjectAcl actions for the S3 bucket.
options.B: In the Account B VPC, create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. For the interface VPC endpoint, create a resource policy that allows the s3 GetObject, s3 ListBucket, s3 PutObject, and s3 PutObjectAcl actions for the S3 bucket.
options.C: In the Account B VPC, create an interface VPC endpoint for AWS KMS. For the interface VPC endpoint, create a resource policy that allows the kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, and kms:GenerateDataKey actions for the KMS key. Ensure that privateDNS is turned on for the endpoint.
options.D: In the Account B VPC, create an interface VPC endpoint for AWS KMS. For the interface VPC endpoint, create a resource policy that allows the kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, and kms:GenerateDataKey actions for the KMS key. Ensure that private DNS is turned off for the endpoint.
options.E: In the Account B VPC, verify that the S3 bucket policy allows the s3 PutObjectAcl action for cross-account use. In the Account B VPC, create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. For the gateway VPC endpoint, create a resource policy that allows the s3 GetObject, s3 ListBucket, and s3 PutObject actions for the S3 bucket.

explanations.A: Correct. A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 keeps traffic to the S3 bucket on the AWS network and off the internet, and it works transparently with the standard S3 DNS names so no application code changes are needed. The endpoint resource policy grants the s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket, s3:PutObject, and s3:PutObjectAcl actions required for the cross-account batch processing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 uses endpoint-specific DNS names, which typically requires changing the application configuration to use them. Because the requirement prohibits changing the system's code, the gateway VPC endpoint in option A is the appropriate choice for private, transparent S3 access.
explanations.C: Correct. AWS KMS is accessed through an interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink), which keeps KMS traffic on the AWS network. Enabling private DNS lets the EC2 instances resolve the standard KMS endpoint to the private endpoint with no code changes, and the resource policy grants the required kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, and kms:GenerateDataKey actions.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Turning off private DNS means the instances cannot resolve the standard AWS KMS endpoint name over the private network without code changes, so KMS calls would not transparently use the interface endpoint. This violates the no-internet, no-code-change requirements.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Although a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 is correct, this option only addresses S3 and omits the AWS KMS interface endpoint needed to encrypt and decrypt the objects privately. It does not keep KMS traffic off the internet, so it is not one of the required steps.

question: A security engineer is designing an IAM policy for a script that will use the AWS CLI. The script currently assumes an IAM role that is attached to three AWS managed IAM policies: AmazonEC2FullAccess, AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess, and AmazonVPCFullAccess. The security engineer needs to construct a least privilege IAM policy that will replace the AWS managed IAM policies that are attached to this role. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: In AWS CloudTrail, create a trail for management events. Run the script with the existing AWS managed IAM policies. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate a new IAM policy that is based on access activity in the trail. Replace the existing AWS managed IAM policies with the generated IAM policy for the role.
options.B: Remove the existing AWS managed IAM policies from the role. Attach the IAM Access Analyzer Role Policy Generator to the role. Run the script. Return to IAM Access Analyzer and generate a least privilege IAM policy. Attach the new IAM policy to the role.
options.C: Create an account analyzer in IAM Access Analyzer. Create an archive rule that has a filter that checks whether the PrincipalArn value matches the ARN of the role. Run the script. Remove the existing AWS managed IAM policies from the role.
options.D: In AWS CloudTrail, create a trail for management events. Remove the existing AWS managed IAM policies from the role. Run the script. Find the authorization failure in the trail event that is associated with the script. Create a new IAM policy that includes the action and resource that caused the authorization failure. Repeat the process until the script succeeds. Attach the new IAM policy to the role.

explanations.A: Correct. Running the script with the existing AWS managed policies while a CloudTrail trail records the management events, then using IAM Access Analyzer to generate a policy based on that access activity, produces a least-privilege policy efficiently. This is the most operationally efficient approach.
explanations.B: Incorrect. There is no such feature as an "IAM Access Analyzer Role Policy Generator" that you attach to a role; this describes functionality that does not exist in AWS, so the option is invalid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Creating an account analyzer and an archive rule that filters on PrincipalArn does not generate a least-privilege policy based on the script's actual access activity, so it does not meet the requirement.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Removing the policies and repeatedly running the script to find and fix each authorization failure is a slow, manual, trial-and-error process. It is far less operationally efficient than generating the policy with IAM Access Analyzer.

question: A security engineer is designing a cloud architecture to support an application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and processes sensitive information, including credit card numbers. The application will send the credit card numbers to a component that is running in an isolated environment. The component will encrypt, store, and decrypt the numbers. The component then will issue tokens to replace the numbers in other parts of the application. The component of the application that manages the tokenization process will be deployed on a separate set of EC2 instances. Other components of the application must not be able to store or access the credit card numbers.Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use EC2 Dedicated Instances for the tokenization component of the application.
options.B: Place the EC2 instances that manage the tokenization process into a partition placement group.
options.C: Create a separate VPDeploy new EC2 instances into the separate VPC to support the data tokenization.
options.D: Deploy the tokenization code onto AWS Nitro Enclaves that are hosted on EC2 instances.

explanations.A: Incorrect. EC2 Dedicated Instances provide physical isolation of hardware but do not provide the logical isolation or encryption needed to ensure other components cannot access the sensitive credit card numbers.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Partition placement groups distribute instances to reduce the impact of correlated hardware failures; they have nothing to do with data isolation or protecting sensitive data from other components.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A separate VPC provides network isolation but does not by itself guarantee that other components cannot access the credit card numbers, nor does it provide the secure encryption and storage the component requires.
explanations.D: Correct. AWS Nitro Enclaves provide a highly isolated, hardened compute environment designed for processing highly sensitive data. The enclave can encrypt, store, and decrypt the card numbers while ensuring that no other component, including the parent EC2 instance, can access them.

question: A company has two AWS accounts: Account A and Account B. Account A has an IAM role that IAM users in Account B assume when they need to upload sensitive documents to Amazon S3 buckets in Account A. A new requirement mandates that users can assume the role only if they are authenticated with multi-factor authentication MFA . A security engineer must recommend a solution that meets this requirement with minimum risk and effort. Which solution should the security engineer recommend?

options.A: Add an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition to the role's permissions policy.
options.B: Add an aws MultiFactorAuthPresent condition to the role ʼ s trust policy.
options.C: Add an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition to the session policy.
options.D: Add an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition to the S3 bucket policies.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A permissions policy defines the actions the role is allowed to perform, but it cannot control who is permitted to assume the role. The MFA requirement must be enforced in the role's trust policy, not in its permissions policy.
explanations.B: Correct. The trust policy defines who can assume the role and under which conditions. Adding an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition to the trust policy ensures that only users authenticated with MFA can assume the role, meeting the requirement with minimal risk and effort.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A session policy further restricts the permissions of an already assumed role; it does not govern who is allowed to assume the role. The MFA assumption requirement cannot be enforced through a session policy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. S3 bucket policies control access to the bucket and its objects, not who is allowed to assume the IAM role. The MFA requirement for assuming the role must be defined in the role's trust policy.

question: A company wants to receive automated email notifications when AWS access keys from developer AWS accounts are detected on code repository sites. Which solution will provide the required email notifications?

options.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to send Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) email notifications for Amazon GuardDuty UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/lnstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS findings.
options.B: Change the AWS account contact information for the Operations type to a separate email address. Periodically poll this email address for notifications.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS Health events that have a value of Risk for the service category. Configure email notifications by using Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS .
options.D: Implement new anomaly detection software. Ingest AWS CloudTrail logs. Configure monitoring for ConsoleLogin events in the AWS Management Console. Configure email notifications from the anomaly detection software.

explanations.A: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty detects credential exfiltration and produces the UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS finding. An Amazon EventBridge rule can match this GuardDuty finding and trigger an Amazon SNS topic to send email notifications, fully meeting the requirement.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Changing the account contact information to a separate email address and periodically polling that mailbox is a manual process. It provides no automated detection of leaked developer access keys and does not use GuardDuty or EventBridge.
explanations.C: Incorrect. AWS Health events report service health and account-level operational issues, not exposed access keys. This approach does not detect credentials found on code repository sites and cannot satisfy the requirement.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Building custom anomaly detection on CloudTrail ConsoleLogin events is complex and monitors console sign-ins, not access keys detected on code repository sites. It does not use GuardDuty or EventBridge and is unnecessarily heavy.

question: A company deployed an Amazon EC2 instance to a VPC on AWS. A recent alert indicates that the EC2 instance is receiving a suspicious number of requests over an open TCP port from an external source. The TCP port remains open for long periods of time. The company's security team needs to stop all activity to this port from the external source to ensure that the EC2 instance is not being compromised. The application must remain available to other users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Update the network ACL that is attached to the subnet that is associated with the EC2 instance. Add a Deny statement for the port and the source IP addresses.
options.B: Update the elastic network interface security group that is attached to the EC2 instance to remove the port from the inbound rule list.
options.C: Update the elastic network interface security group that is attached to the EC2 instance by adding a Deny entry in the inbound list for the port and the source IP addresses.
options.D: Create a new network ACL for the subnet. Deny all traffic from the EC2 instance to prevent data from being removed

explanations.A: Correct. Network ACLs support explicit Deny rules. Adding a Deny statement for the specific port and the malicious source IP addresses on the subnet's network ACL blocks that traffic precisely while allowing all other users to continue reaching the application.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Removing the port from the security group inbound rules blocks all inbound traffic on that port, not just traffic from the malicious source, so the application would no longer be available to other legitimate users.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Security groups do not support explicit Deny rules; they only allow traffic through allow rules. Adding a Deny entry to a security group is not technically possible, so this option is invalid.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Denying all traffic makes the application unavailable to everyone, which contradicts the requirement that the application must remain available to other users.

question: A company has secured the AWS account root user for its AWS account by following AWS best practices. The company also has enabled AWS CloudTrail, which is sending its logs to Amazon S3. A security engineer wants to receive notification in near-real time if a user uses the AWS account root user credentials to sign in to the AWS Management Console Which solutions will provide this notification? Choose two.)

options.A: Use AWS Trusted Advisor and its security evaluations for the root account. Configure an Amazon EventBridge event rule that is invoked by the Trusted Advisor API. Configure the rule to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe any required endpoints to the SNS topic so that these endpoints can receive notification.
options.B: Use AWS IAM Access Analyzer. Create an Amazon Cloud Watch Logs metric filter to evaluate log entries from Access Analyzer that detect a successful root account login. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors whether a root login has occurred. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic when the alarm enters the ALARM state. Subscribe any required endpoints to this SNS topic so that these endpoints can receive notification.
options.C: Configure AWS CloudTrail to send its logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure a metric filter on the CloudWatch Logs log group used by CloudTrail to evaluate log entries for successful root account logins. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors whether a root login has occurred. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic when the alarm enters the ALARM state. Subscribe any required endpoints to this SNS topic so that these endpoints can receive notification.
options.D: Configure AWS CloudTrail to send log notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function that parses the CloudTrail notification for root login activity and notifies a separate SNS topic that contains the endpoints that should receive notification. Subscribe the Lambda function to the SNS topic that is receiving log notifications from CloudTrail.
options.E: Configure an Amazon EventBridge event rule that runs when Amazon CloudWatch API calls are recorded for a successful root login. Configure the rule to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe any required endpoints to the SNS topic so that these endpoints can receive notification.

explanations.A: Incorrect. AWS Trusted Advisor provides account security recommendations but does not detect root user sign-in events in near-real time, and its API cannot trigger an EventBridge rule to react to a console login.
explanations.B: Incorrect. AWS IAM Access Analyzer evaluates resource access and permissions, not sign-in activity. It does not generate log entries for successful root logins, so a metric filter on Access Analyzer output cannot detect a root sign-in.
explanations.C: Correct. CloudTrail records root user console sign-in events. Sending CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs, creating a metric filter for successful root logins, and configuring a CloudWatch alarm to notify an SNS topic delivers near-real-time notification.
explanations.D: Incorrect. CloudTrail's SNS integration only announces that a new log file has been delivered; it does not send the parsed login event itself. Building a Lambda function to parse those notifications is more complex than required and is not the recommended pattern.
explanations.E: Correct. An Amazon EventBridge rule can match the CloudTrail-recorded console sign-in event for the root user and target an SNS topic, providing near-real-time notification whenever the root credentials are used to sign in.

question: A company has AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. A security engineer needs to set up AWS Security Hub in a dedicated account for security monitoring. The security engineer must ensure that Security Hub automatically manages all existing accounts and all new accounts that are added to the organization. Security Hub also must receive findings from all AWS Regions. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? Choose two.)

options.A: Configure a finding aggregation Region for Security Hub. Link the other Regions to the aggregation Region.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that routes events from other Regions to the dedicated Security Hub account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function.
options.C: Turn on the option to automatically enable accounts for Security Hub.
options.D: Create an SCP that denies the securityhub:DisableSecurityHub permission. Attach the SCP to the organization ʼ s root account.
options.E: Configure services in other Regions to write events to an AWS CloudTrail organization trail. Configure Security Hub to read events from the trail.

explanations.A: Correct. Configuring a finding aggregation Region in Security Hub and linking the other Regions consolidates findings from all Regions into one aggregation Region. This is the recommended best practice and adds little operational overhead.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Building an AWS Lambda function plus an EventBridge rule to route events between Regions requires custom development and ongoing maintenance, which increases operational overhead and does not meet the LEAST operational overhead requirement.
explanations.C: Correct. Turning on the option to automatically enable accounts for Security Hub causes Security Hub to manage all existing accounts and any new accounts added to the organization automatically, meeting the requirement with the least effort.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An SCP that denies securityhub:DisableSecurityHub only prevents accounts from disabling Security Hub; it does not automatically enable Security Hub across accounts or aggregate findings from all Regions, so it does not meet the requirements.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Security Hub does not rely on a CloudTrail organization trail to read events. This approach does not automatically enable accounts or aggregate Security Hub findings across Regions and does not match the requirement.

question: A security engineer is implementing a solution to allow users to seamlessly encrypt Amazon S3 objects without having to touch the keys directly. The solution must be highly scalable without requiring continual management. Additionally, the organization must be able to immediately delete the encryption keys. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS KMS with AWS managed keys and the ScheduleKeyDeletion API with a PendingWindowInDays set to 0 to remove the keys if necessary.
options.B: Use KMS with AWS imported key material and then use the DeleteImportedKeyMaterial API to remove the key material if necessary.
options.C: Use AWS CloudHSM to store the keys and then use the CloudHSM API or the PKCS11 library to delete the keys if necessary.
options.D: Use the Systems Manager Parameter Store to store the keys and then use the service API operations to delete the keys if necessary.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The KMS ScheduleKeyDeletion API does not accept a PendingWindowInDays value of 0; the minimum waiting period is 7 days, so it cannot satisfy the requirement to delete the encryption keys immediately.
explanations.B: Correct. Using AWS KMS with imported key material lets you call the DeleteImportedKeyMaterial API to remove the key material immediately, meeting the immediate-deletion requirement while KMS remains highly scalable and requires no continual management.
explanations.C: Incorrect. AWS CloudHSM can store and delete keys, but it requires significant ongoing management and operational complexity, which does not meet the requirement for a highly scalable solution without continual management.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Systems Manager Parameter Store is designed to store parameters and configuration data, not to serve as a key management service. It does not provide seamless, scalable encryption of Amazon S3 objects.

question: A company needs to implement DNS Security Extensions DNSSEC) for a specific subdomain. The subdomain is already registered with Amazon Route 53. A security engineer has enabled DNSSEC signing and has created a key- signing key KSK . When the security engineer tries to test the configuration, the security engineer receives an error for a broken trust chain. What should the security engineer do to resolve this error?

options.A: Replace the KSK with a zone-signing key ZSK .
options.B: Deactivate and then activate the KSK.
options.C: Create a Delegation Signer DS) record in the parent hosted zone.
options.D: Create a Delegation Signer DS) record in the subdomain.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The KSK and ZSK serve different purposes: the KSK signs the key set that is referenced by the DS record, while the ZSK signs the zone data. Replacing the KSK with a ZSK does not repair the broken chain of trust.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Deactivating and then reactivating the KSK does not fix the chain of trust, because the root cause is the missing DS record in the parent, not the state of the KSK.
explanations.C: Correct. The chain of trust is established by creating a Delegation Signer (DS) record in the parent hosted zone. Without the DS record in the parent, the parent cannot validate the subdomain's DNSSEC signatures and the chain of trust is broken.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The DS record must be created in the parent hosted zone, not in the subdomain itself. Placing a DS record in the subdomain does not establish the chain of trust with the parent.

question: A company used AWS Organizations to set up an environment with multiple AWS accounts. The company's organization currently has two AWS accounts, and the company expects to add more than 50 AWS accounts during the next 12 months. The company will require all existing and future AWS accounts to use Amazon GuardDuty. Each existing AWS account has GuardDuty active. The company reviews GuardDuty findings by logging into each AWS account individually. The company wants a centralized view of the GuardDuty findings for the existing AWS accounts and any future AWS accounts. The company also must ensure that any new AWS account has GuardDuty automatically turned on. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Enable AWS Security Hub in the organization's management account. Configure GuardDuty within the management account to send all GuardDuty findings to Security Hub.
options.B: Create a new AWS account in the organization. Enable GuardDuty in the new account. Designate the new account as the delegated administrator account for GuardDuty. Configure GuardDuty to add existing accounts as member accounts. Select the option to automatically add new AWS accounts to the organization.
options.C: Create a new AWS account in the organization. Enable GuardDuty in the new account. Enable AWS Security Hub in each account. Select the option to automatically add new AWS accounts to the organization.
options.D: Enable AWS Security Hub in the organization's management account. Designate the management account as the delegated administrator account for Security Hub. Add existing accounts as member accounts. Select the option to automatically add new AWS accounts to the organization. Send all Security Hub findings to the organization's GuardDuty account.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Enabling Security Hub in the management account and forwarding GuardDuty findings does not provide centralized GuardDuty administration, and it does not automatically turn on GuardDuty in newly added accounts.
explanations.B: Correct. Creating a new account, designating it as the GuardDuty delegated administrator, adding the existing accounts as member accounts, and selecting the option to auto-enable new organization accounts centralizes the GuardDuty findings and automatically turns on GuardDuty for every new account.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Enabling GuardDuty in a new account and Security Hub in each account does not provide centralized GuardDuty administration, and it does not automatically enable GuardDuty for new accounts.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This option focuses on Security Hub delegated administration and sending Security Hub findings to a GuardDuty account, which does not meet the requirement for centralized GuardDuty management and automatic GuardDuty enablement.

question: A company wants to remove all SSH keys permanently from a specific subset of its Amazon Linux 2 Amazon EC2 instances that are using the same IAM instance profile. However, three individuals who have IAM user accounts will need to access these instances by using an SSH session to perform critical duties. How can a security engineer provide the access to meet these requirements?

options.A: Assign an IAM policy to the instance profile to allow the EC2 instances to be managed by AWS Systems Manager. Provide the IAM user accounts with permission to use Systems Manager. Remove the SSH keys from the EC2 instances. Use Systems Manager Inventory to select the EC2 instance and connect.
options.B: Assign an IAM policy to the IAM user accounts to provide permission to use AWS Systems Manager Run Command. Remove the SSH keys from the EC2 instances. Use Run Command to open an SSH connection to the EC2 instance.
options.C: Assign an IAM policy to the instance profile to allow the EC2 instances to be managed by AWS Systems Manager. Provide the IAM user accounts with permission to use Systems Manager. Remove the SSH keys from the EC2 instances. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to select the EC2 instance and connect.
options.D: Assign an IAM policy to the IAM user accounts to provide permission to use the EC2 service in the AWS Management Console. Remove the SSH keys from the EC2 instances. Connect to the EC2 instance as the ec2-user through the AWS Management Console ʼ s EC2 SSH client method.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Systems Manager Inventory collects metadata about instances; it cannot be used to open an interactive session or connect to an EC2 instance, so it does not satisfy the SSH access requirement.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Systems Manager Run Command executes commands on instances but does not provide an interactive shell session, so it cannot replace the SSH access the three users need.
explanations.C: Correct. Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure interactive shell access without SSH keys. Granting the instance profile permission to be managed by Systems Manager and giving the IAM users Session Manager permissions lets them connect after the SSH keys are removed.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The AWS Management Console does not offer a native EC2 SSH client to connect as ec2-user once the SSH keys have been removed; the method described does not exist.

question: A company is storing data in Amazon S3 Glacier. A security engineer implemented a new vault lock policy for 10 TB of data and called the initiate- vault-lock operation 12 hours ago. The audit team identified a typo in the policy that is allowing unintended access to the vault. What is the MOST cost-effective way to correct this error?

options.A: Call the abort-vault-lock operation. Update the policy. Call the initiate-vault- lock operation again.
options.B: Copy the vault data to a new S3 bucket. Delete the vault Create a new vault with the data.
options.C: Update the policy to keep the vault lock in place.
options.D: Update the policy. Call the initiate-vault-lock operation again to apply the new policy.

explanations.A: Correct. The vault lock process has two stages: initiate and complete. Before completion (within the 24-hour window), you can call abort-vault-lock to stop the in-progress lock, update the policy to fix the typo, and call initiate-vault-lock again. This is the most cost-effective fix because no data must be copied or recreated.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Copying 10 TB of data to a new S3 bucket and recreating the vault incurs additional storage and data transfer charges and adds unnecessary complexity, so it is not cost-effective.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Once a vault lock is complete the policy is immutable and cannot be updated in place. This option ignores that the lock is still in progress and can simply be aborted.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Calling initiate-vault-lock again without first aborting the in-progress lock does not work. You must call abort-vault-lock to stop the current lock before re-initiating with the corrected policy.

question: A company uses HTTP Live Streaming HLS) to stream live video content to paying subscribers by using Amazon CloudFront. HLS splits the video content into chunks so that the user can request the right chunk based on different conditions. Because the video events last for several hours, the total video is made up of thousands of chunks. The origin URL is not disclosed, and every user is forced to access the CloudFront URL. The company has a web application that authenticates the paying users against an internal repository and a CloudFront key pair that is already issued. What is the simplest and MOST effective way to protect the content?

options.A: Develop the application to use the CloudFront key pair to create signed URLs that users will use to access the content.
options.B: Develop the application to use the CloudFront key pair to set the signed cookies that users will use to access the content.
options.C: Develop the application to issue a security token that Lambda@Edge will receive to authenticate and authorize access to the content.
options.D: Keep the CloudFront URL encrypted inside the application, and use AWS KMS to resolve the URL on-the-fly after the user is authenticated.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Signed URLs can protect the content, but with HLS the video is split into thousands of chunks and each chunk URL would have to be signed individually, adding significant management complexity and overhead. It is not the simplest or most effective approach.
explanations.B: Correct. CloudFront signed cookies can authorize access to many files at once, so a single set of cookies covers all the HLS chunks for the user's session without signing each chunk URL individually. This is the simplest and most effective way to protect HLS content.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Using Lambda@Edge with a security token is flexible but requires additional development and ongoing maintenance to implement, making it more complex than signed cookies and not the simplest solution.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Encrypting the CloudFront URL in the application and using AWS KMS to resolve it on the fly adds complexity and cost and does not effectively protect the many individual HLS chunks.

question: A company runs workloads in the us-east-1 Region. The company has never deployed resources to other AWS Regions and does not have any multi-Region resources. The company needs to replicate its workloads and infrastructure to the us-west-1 Region. A security engineer must implement a solution that uses AWS Secrets Manager to store secrets in both Regions. The solution must use AWS Key Management Service AWS KMS) to encrypt the secrets. The solution must minimize latency and must be able to work if only one Region is available. The security engineer uses Secrets Manager to create the secrets in us-east-1. What should the security engineer do next to meet the requirements?

options.A: Encrypt the secrets in us-east-1 by using an AWS managed KMS key. Replicate the secrets to us-west-1. Encrypt the secrets in us-west-1 by using a new AWS managed KMS key in us-west-1.
options.B: Encrypt the secrets in us-east-1 by using an AWS managed KMS key. Configure resources in us-west-1 to call the Secrets Manager endpoint in us- east-1.
options.C: Encrypt the secrets in us-east-1 by using a customer managed KMS key. Configure resources in us-west-1 to call the Secrets Manager endpoint in us- east-1.
options.D: Encrypt the secrets in us-east-1 by using a customer managed KMS key. Replicate the secrets to us-west-1. Encrypt the secrets in us-west-1 by using the customer managed KMS key from us-east-1.

explanations.A: Incorrect. AWS managed KMS keys cannot be used across Regions; each Region's AWS managed key is independent, so you cannot encrypt the replicated secret in us-west-1 with the same key, and using different managed keys does not satisfy the requirement.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Having us-west-1 resources call the Secrets Manager endpoint in us-east-1 adds cross-Region latency and fails entirely if us-east-1 becomes unavailable, violating both the minimize-latency and single-Region-availability requirements.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Using a customer managed key does not help here because resources in us-west-1 still call the us-east-1 endpoint, which adds cross-Region latency and fails if us-east-1 is unavailable, just like option B.
explanations.D: Correct. Encrypt the secret in us-east-1 with a customer managed KMS key, replicate the secret to us-west-1, and encrypt the replica with the customer managed key. Because each Region has its own local Secrets Manager replica, latency is minimized and the solution keeps working even if one Region is unavailable.

question: A company operates a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application listens on port 80 and port 443. The company uses an Application Load Balancer ALB) with AWS WAF to terminate SSL and to forward traffic to the application instances only on port 80. The ALB is in public subnets that are associated with a network ACL that is named NACL1. The application instances are in dedicated private subnets that are associated with a network ACL that is named NACL2. An Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance that uses port 5432 is in a dedicated private subnet that is associated with a network ACL that is named NACL3. All the network ACLs currently allow all inbound and outbound traffic. Which set of network ACL changes will increase the security of the application while ensuring functionality?

options.A: Make the following changes to NACL3 • Add a rule that allows inbound traffic on port 5432 from NACL2. • Add a rule that allows outbound traffic on ports 1024 65536 to NACL2. • Remove the default rules that allow all inbound and outbound traffic.
options.B: Make the following changes to NACL3 • Add a rule that allows inbound traffic on port 5432 from the Cl DR blocks of the application instance subnets. • Add a rule that allows outbound traffic on ports 1024 65536 to the application instance subnets. • Remove the default rules that allow all inbound and outbound traffic.
options.C: Make the following changes to NACL2 • Add a rule that allows outbound traffic on port 5432 to the CIDR blocks of the RDS subnets. • Remove the default rules that allow all inbound and outbound traffic.
options.D: Make the following changes to NACL2 • Add a rule that allows inbound traffic on port 5432 from the CIDR blocks of the RDS subnets. • Add a rule that allows outbound traffic on port 5432 to the RDS subnets.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Network ACL rules are evaluated against CIDR blocks, not against other network ACLs by name. Referencing NACL2 as a source is invalid; the inbound rule on NACL3 must reference the application instance subnet CIDR blocks.
explanations.B: Correct. NACL3 protects the RDS subnet. Allowing inbound port 5432 from the application instance subnet CIDR blocks, allowing outbound ephemeral ports (1024-65535) back to those subnets, and removing the allow-all default rules secures the database tier while preserving required connectivity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Changing only NACL2 to allow outbound traffic to the RDS subnets, without corresponding inbound rules, leaves the configuration incomplete and does not properly secure the tiers while ensuring functionality.
explanations.D: Incorrect. NACL2 protects the application instance subnet, not the RDS subnet. Adding inbound port 5432 from the RDS subnets to NACL2 is the wrong placement and direction and does not correctly secure the database tier.

question: AWS CloudTrail is being used to monitor API calls in an organization. An audit revealed that CloudTrail is failing to deliver events to Amazon S3 as expected. What initial actions should be taken to allow delivery of CloudTrail events to S3? Choose two.)

options.A: Verify that the S3 bucket policy allows CloudTrail to write objects.
options.B: Verify that the IAM role used by CloudTrail has access to write to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
options.C: Remove any lifecycle policies on the S3 bucket that are archiving objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
options.D: Verify that the S3 bucket defined in CloudTrail exists.
options.E: Verify that the log file prefix defined in CloudTrail exists in the S3 bucket.

explanations.A: Correct. CloudTrail requires an S3 bucket policy that permits the CloudTrail service to write (put) objects. If the bucket policy does not allow CloudTrail to write, log files cannot be delivered to S3.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The problem is delivery of events to S3, not to CloudWatch Logs. The IAM role used for CloudWatch Logs integration is unrelated to why events are not reaching the S3 bucket.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lifecycle policies that archive objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval only change the storage class of existing objects; they do not affect the delivery of new CloudTrail events to the bucket.
explanations.D: Correct. If the S3 bucket configured in the CloudTrail trail does not exist, CloudTrail cannot deliver events to it. Verifying that the configured bucket actually exists is an appropriate initial action.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The log file prefix is only a logical path within the bucket and does not need to exist in advance. A missing prefix does not prevent CloudTrail from delivering events to S3.

question: A company has public certificates that are managed by AWS Certificate Manager ACM . The certificates are either imported certificates or managed certificates from ACM with mixed validation methods. A security engineer needs to design a monitoring solution to provide alerts by email when a certificate is approaching its expiration date. What is the MOST operationally efficient way to meet this requirement?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to list all certificates and to go through each certificate to describe the certificate by using the AWS SDK. Filter on the NotAfter attribute and send an email notification. Use an Amazon EventBridge rate expression to schedule the Lambda function to run daily.
options.B: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm. Add all the certificate ARNs in the AWS/CertificateManager namespace to the DaysToExpiry metric. Configure the alarm to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS topic when the value for the DaysToExpiry metric is less than or equal to 31.
options.C: Set up AWS Security Hub. Turn on the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard with integrated ACM to send findings. Configure and use a custom action by creating a rule to match the pattern from the ACM findings on the NotBefore attribute as the event source. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic as the target.
options.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule by using a predefined pattern for ACM Choose the metric in the ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration event as the event pattern. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A custom Lambda function that lists and describes every certificate, filters on the NotAfter attribute, and sends email works, but it requires writing and maintaining code plus a scheduled invocation, which is more operational overhead than necessary.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The CloudWatch DaysToExpiry metric applies only to ACM-issued (managed) certificates and does not cover imported certificates, so it cannot monitor all of the company's certificates.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Security Hub with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard focuses on overall security posture and compliance rather than certificate expiration alerts, and it requires extra configuration and integration.
explanations.D: Correct. An Amazon EventBridge rule using the predefined "ACM Certificate Approaching Expiration" event pattern, targeting an SNS topic, notifies you of upcoming expirations for both imported and managed certificates with no custom code and the least operational effort.

question: A security team is responsible for reviewing AWS API call activity in the cloud environment for security violations. These events must be recorded and retained in a centralized location for both current and future AWS regions. What is the SIMPLEST way to meet these requirements?

options.A: Enable AWS Trusted Advisor security checks in the AWS Console, and report all security incidents for all regions.
options.B: Enable AWS CloudTrail by creating individual trails for each region, and specify a single Amazon S3 bucket to receive log files for later analysis.
options.C: Enable AWS CloudTrail by creating a new trail and applying the trail to all regions. Specify a single Amazon S3 bucket as the storage location.
options.D: Enable Amazon CloudWatch logging for all AWS services across all regions, and aggregate them to a single Amazon S3 bucket for later analysis.

explanations.A: Incorrect. AWS Trusted Advisor provides optimization recommendations for cost, performance, and security; it does not record API call activity and cannot centrally store API logs for auditing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Creating a separate CloudTrail trail for each Region works but is unnecessarily complex to manage. CloudTrail supports a single multi-Region trail that accomplishes the same result more simply.
explanations.C: Correct. Creating one CloudTrail trail applied to all Regions and specifying a single S3 bucket as the destination records API activity across current and future Regions in one central location. This is the simplest solution that meets the requirements.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Amazon CloudWatch is used to monitor metrics and the operational state of services, not to record API call activity. CloudTrail is the appropriate service for capturing AWS API calls.

question: A company is running an application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application stores logs locally. A security engineer noticed that logs were lost after a scale-in event. The security engineer needs to recommend a solution to ensure the durability and availability of log data. All logs must be kept for a minimum of 1 year for auditing purposes. What should the security engineer recommend?

options.A: Within the Auto Scaling lifecycle, add a hook to create and attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store Amazon EBS) log volume each time an EC2 instance is created. When the instance is terminated, the EBS volume can be reattached to another instance for log review.
options.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System Amazon EFS) file system and add a command in the user data section of the Auto Scaling launch template to mount the EFS file system during EC2 instance creation. Configure a process on the instance to copy the logs once a day from an instance Amazon Elastic Block Store Amazon EBS) volume to a directory in the EFS file system.
options.C: Add an Amazon CloudWatch agent into the AMI used in the Auto Scaling group. Configure the CloudWatch agent to send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for review.
options.D: Within the Auto Scaling lifecycle, add a lifecycle hook at the terminating state transition and alert the engineering team by using a lifecycle notification to Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS . Configure the hook to remain in the Terminating:Wait state for 1 hour to allow manual review of the security logs prior to instance termination.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Creating and attaching a per-instance EBS log volume and reattaching it after termination is complex, difficult to automate at scale, and error-prone, so it does not reliably ensure log durability.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mounting EFS and copying logs only once a day from an EBS volume adds complexity and can lose logs, for example when an instance terminates suddenly before the daily copy runs, so it does not guarantee durability.
explanations.C: Correct. Installing the CloudWatch agent in the AMI and configuring it to stream logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs sends log data in near real time and stores it independently of the instance lifecycle, ensuring durability and availability. CloudWatch Logs retention can be set to keep logs for at least one year.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A terminating-state lifecycle hook with an SNS notification and a Terminating:Wait period relies on manual review before termination and does not durably or automatically persist the logs, so logs can still be lost.

question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances to host frontend services behind an Application Load Balancer. Amazon Elastic Block Store Amazon EBS) volumes are attached to the EC2 instances. The company uses Amazon S3 buckets to store large files for images and music. The company has implemented a security architecture on AWS to prevent, identify, and isolate potential ransomware attacks. The company now wants to further reduce risk. A security engineer must develop a disaster recovery solution that can recover to normal operations if an attacker bypasses preventive and detective controls. The solution must meet an RPO of 1 hour. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Backup to create backups of the EC2 instances and S3 buckets every hour. Create AWS CloudFormation templates that replicate existing architecture components. Use AWS CodeCommit to store the CloudFormation templates alongside application configuration code.
options.B: Use AWS Backup to create backups of the EBS volumes and S3 objects every day. Use Amazon Security Lake to create a centralized data lake for AWS CloudTrail logs and VPC flow logs. Use the logs for automated response.
options.C: Use Amazon Security Lake to create a centralized data lake for AWS CloudTrail logs and VPC flow logs. Use the logs for automated response. Enable AWS Security Hub to establish a single location for recovery procedures. Create AWS CloudFormation templates that replicate existing architecture components. Use AWS CodeCommit to store the CloudFormation templates alongside application configuration code.
options.D: Create EBS snapshots every 4 hours. Enable Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Create automation to immediately restore the most recent snapshot for any EC2 instances that produce an Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile finding in GuardDuty.

explanations.A: Correct. Using AWS Backup to back up the EC2 instances and S3 buckets every hour meets the 1-hour RPO. AWS CloudFormation templates replicate the architecture components, and storing them in AWS CodeCommit alongside application configuration provides version-controlled, automated recovery.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Daily backups of the EBS volumes and S3 objects cannot meet a 1-hour RPO, and Amazon Security Lake is a detection and response service rather than a disaster recovery solution.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Amazon Security Lake and AWS Security Hub focus on detection and response, and this option includes no scheduled backups, so it cannot meet the 1-hour RPO required for recovery.
explanations.D: Incorrect. EBS snapshots taken every 4 hours cannot meet a 1-hour RPO, and Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection is a detection and response tool rather than a disaster recovery solution.

question: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer ALB . The instances are in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group and are attached to Amazon Elastic Block Store Amazon EBS) volumes. A security engineer needs to preserve all forensic evidence from one of the instances. Which order of steps should the security engineer use to meet this requirement?

options.A: Take an EBS volume snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an Amazon S3 bucket. Take a memory snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an S3 bucket Detach the instance from the Auto Scaling group. Deregister the instance from the ALB. Stop the instance.
options.B: Take a memory snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an Amazon S3 bucket. Stop the instance. Take an EBS volume snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an S3 bucket. Detach the instance from the Auto Scaling group. Deregister the instance from the ALB.
options.C: Detach the instance from the Auto Scaling group. Deregister the instance from the ALB. Take an EBS volume snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an Amazon S3 bucket. Take a memory snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an S3 bucket. Stop the instance.
options.D: Detach the instance from the Auto Scaling group. Deregister the instance from the ALB Stop the instance. Take a memory snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an Amazon S3 bucket. Take an EBS volume snapshot of the instance and store the snapshot in an S3 bucket.

explanations.A: Incorrect. This sequence takes the EBS volume snapshot and memory snapshot first, but it does not isolate the instance before capturing evidence. Because the instance is still attached to the Auto Scaling group and registered with the ALB, Auto Scaling could terminate or replace it and live traffic could keep hitting it during acquisition, compromising the evidence.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Capturing the memory snapshot before stopping the instance is correct, but the instance is never detached from the Auto Scaling group or deregistered from the ALB before acquisition. This leaves the instance exposed to replacement by Auto Scaling and to continued traffic, which can alter or destroy forensic evidence.
explanations.C: Correct. The instance is first detached from the Auto Scaling group and deregistered from the ALB so it cannot be replaced or continue receiving traffic. Evidence is then preserved by taking the EBS volume snapshot and the memory snapshot while the instance is still running, and the instance is stopped last. This is the correct forensic order.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Detaching from the Auto Scaling group and deregistering from the ALB first is right, but the instance is stopped before the memory snapshot is taken. Volatile memory cannot be captured after the instance is stopped, so the memory evidence would be lost.

question: An application team wants to use AWS Certificate Manager ACM) to request public certificates to ensure that data is secured in transit. The domains that are being used are not currently hosted on Amazon Route 53. The application team wants to use an AWS managed distribution and caching solution to optimize requests to its systems and provide better points of presence to customers. The distribution solution will use a primary domain name that is customized. The distribution solution also will use several alternative domain names. The certificates must renew automatically over an indefinite period of time. Which combination of steps should the application team take to deploy this architecture? Choose three.)

options.A: Request a certificate from ACM in the us-west-2 Region. Add the domain names that the certificate will secure.
options.B: Send an email message to the domain administrators to request validation of the domains for ACM.
options.C: Request validation of the domains for ACM through DNS. Insert CNAME records into each domain's DNS zone.
options.D: Create an Application Load Balancer for the caching solution. Select the newly requested certificate from ACM to be used for secure connections.
options.E: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the caching solution. Enter the main CNAME record as the Origin Name.Enter the subdomain names or alternate names in the Alternate Domain Names Distribution Settings. Select the newly requested certificate from ACM to be used for secure connections.
options.F: Request a certificate from ACM in the us-east-1 Region. Add the domain names that the certificate will secure.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A public certificate that will be used with Amazon CloudFront must be requested from ACM in the us-east-1 Region. A certificate requested in us-west-2 cannot be associated with a CloudFront distribution.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Email validation requires manual action from domain administrators and does not support the automatic, indefinite renewal that this requirement calls for. DNS validation with CNAME records is what allows ACM to renew the certificate automatically over an indefinite period.
explanations.C: Correct. Because the domains are not hosted on Amazon Route 53, DNS validation is performed by inserting the ACM-provided CNAME record into each domain's DNS zone. DNS validation lets ACM renew the certificate automatically for an indefinite period of time.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An Application Load Balancer is not the AWS managed distribution and caching solution with global points of presence that the requirement describes. The correct service for this is Amazon CloudFront, not an ALB.
explanations.E: Correct. Amazon CloudFront is the AWS managed distribution and caching solution that provides points of presence to customers. The customized primary domain and the alternative domain names are entered as Alternate Domain Names (CNAMEs), and the ACM certificate is selected to secure the connections.
explanations.F: Correct. The ACM public certificate must be requested in the us-east-1 Region so that it can be used with the Amazon CloudFront distribution.

question: A company ʼ s security engineer wants to receive an email alert whenever Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer, or Amazon Macie generate a high-severity security finding. The company uses AWS Control Tower to govern all of its accounts. The company also uses AWS Security Hub with all of the AWS service integrations turned on. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Set up separate AWS Lambda functions for GuardDuty, IAM Access Analyzer, and Macie to call each service's public API to retrieve high-severity findings. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) to send the email alerts. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the functions on a schedule.
options.B: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with a pattern that matches Security Hub findings events with high severity. Configure the rule to send the findings to a target Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the desired email addresses to the SNS topic.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with a pattern that matches AWS Control Tower events with high severity. Configure the rule to send the findings to a target Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the desired email addresses to the SNS topic.
options.D: Host an application on Amazon EC2 to call the GuardDuty. IAM Access Analyzer, and Macie APIs. Within the application,use the Amazon Simple Notification Service Amazon SNS API to retrieve high-severity findings and to send the findings to an SNS topic. Subscribe the desired email addresses to the SNS topic.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Building separate Lambda functions that poll each service's public API on a schedule adds significant custom code and operational overhead, and scheduled polling is not near-real-time. This does not meet the requirement for the least operational overhead.
explanations.B: Correct. Security Hub already aggregates findings from GuardDuty, IAM Access Analyzer, and Macie. A single Amazon EventBridge rule can match Security Hub findings with high severity and route them to an Amazon SNS topic, and subscribing the email addresses to that topic delivers the alerts. This is the lowest-overhead solution.
explanations.C: Incorrect. AWS Control Tower is used for account governance and does not emit the high-severity security findings from GuardDuty, IAM Access Analyzer, or Macie. Matching Control Tower events would not satisfy the requirement to alert on high-severity security findings.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hosting an application on Amazon EC2 to call each service's API and publish to SNS introduces servers to manage and custom code, which adds operational overhead and cost. This does not meet the least-operational-overhead requirement.

question: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application also uses Amazon S3 and Amazon Simple QueueService Amazon SQS . The application is behind an Application Load Balancer ALB) and scales with AWS Auto Scaling. The company's security policy requires the use of least privilege access, which has been applied to all existing AWS resources. A security engineer needs to implement private connectivity to AWS services. Which combination of steps should the security engineer take to meet this requirement? Choose three.)

options.A: Use an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS.
options.B: Configure a connection to Amazon S3 through AWS Transit Gateway.
options.C: Use a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3.
options.D: Modify the IAM role applied to the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group to allow outbound traffic to the interface endpoints.
options.E: Modify the endpoint policies on all VPC endpoints. Specify the SQS and S3 resources that the application uses.
options.F: Configure a connection to Amazon S3 through AWS Firewall Manager.

explanations.A: Correct. Amazon SQS does not support gateway VPC endpoints, so an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink) is used to provide private connectivity from the VPC to Amazon SQS.
explanations.B: Incorrect. AWS Transit Gateway is used to interconnect VPCs and on-premises networks, not to establish private connectivity to an AWS service such as Amazon S3. Private access to S3 is provided by a gateway VPC endpoint.
explanations.C: Correct. Amazon S3 supports gateway VPC endpoints, which provide private connectivity to S3 from the VPC via route table entries at no additional charge.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An IAM role controls API-level permissions, not network egress. Outbound access to interface endpoints is governed by security groups and route tables, not by editing the instance IAM role, so this step is not what enables private connectivity.
explanations.E: Correct. Applying endpoint policies that specify only the SQS and S3 resources the application uses restricts what can be reached through the VPC endpoints, which enforces the least-privilege access required by the company's security policy.
explanations.F: Incorrect. AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall rules (such as AWS WAF and security group policies) across accounts; it does not create private connectivity to Amazon S3. A gateway VPC endpoint is the correct mechanism for that.

question: 英 ⽂ : A security analyst attempted to troubleshoot the monitoring of suspicious security group changes. The analyst was told that there is an Amazon CloudWatch alarm in place for these AWS CloudTrail log events. The analyst tested the monitoring setup by making a configuration change to the security group but did not receive any alerts. Which of the following troubleshooting steps should the analyst perform?

options.A: Ensure that CloudTrail and S3 bucket access logging is enabled for the analyst's AWS account.
options.B: Verify that a metric filter was created and then mapped to an alarm. Check the alarm notification action.
options.C: Check the CloudWatch dashboards to ensure that there is a metric configured with an appropriate dimension for security group changes.
options.D: Verify that the analyst's account is mapped to an IAM policy that includes permissions for cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics and cloudwatch:ListMetrics.

explanations.A: Incorrect. While CloudTrail must be enabled to capture security group changes, the scenario indicates the monitoring pipeline was already built. S3 bucket access logging records object-level access to S3 buckets and is unrelated to detecting security group changes, so it is not the troubleshooting step to take.
explanations.B: Correct. For CloudTrail events to trigger a CloudWatch alarm, a metric filter must be created on the CloudTrail log group and mapped to a CloudWatch alarm, and the alarm must have a valid notification action. A missing or misconfigured metric filter or notification action is the most likely reason no alert was received.
explanations.C: Incorrect. CloudWatch dashboards are used to visualize metrics; they do not trigger alarms or send notifications. Checking a dashboard would not explain why the alarm failed to alert on the security group change.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics and cloudwatch:ListMetrics permissions let a principal read metric data; they are unrelated to whether an alarm fires and sends a notification. Missing these permissions would not cause the alert to be silent.

question: An Amazon API Gateway API invokes an AWS Lambda function that needs to interact with a software-as-a-service SaaS) platform. A unique client token is generated in the SaaS platform to grant access to the Lambda function. A security engineer needs to design a solution to encrypt the access token at rest and pass the token to the Lambda function at runtime. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Store the client token as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the AWS SDK to retrieve the secret in the Lambda function.
options.B: Configure a token-based Lambda authorizer in API Gateway.
options.C: Store the client token as a SecureString parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Use the AWS SDK to retrieve the value of the SecureString parameter in the Lambda function..
options.D: Use AWS Key Management Service AWS KMS) to encrypt the client token. Pass the token to the Lambda function at runtime through an environment variable.

explanations.A: Incorrect. AWS Secrets Manager can securely store and encrypt the client token and Lambda can retrieve it with the AWS SDK, so this is technically valid. However, Secrets Manager costs more per secret than Parameter Store, so it is not the most cost-effective option.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A token-based Lambda authorizer in API Gateway is used to authorize incoming API requests; it does not encrypt a secret at rest or pass the SaaS client token to the Lambda function at runtime. It does not meet the requirement.
explanations.C: Correct. Storing the token as a SecureString parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store encrypts it at rest with AWS KMS, and the Lambda function can retrieve it at runtime with the AWS SDK. Standard SecureString parameters incur no additional charge, making this the most cost-effective solution.
explanations.D: Incorrect. AWS KMS can encrypt the token, but passing it to the function through a Lambda environment variable risks exposing the sensitive value, and the KMS API calls add cost. This is less secure and not the most cost-effective approach compared with a SecureString parameter.

question: A company is using an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content from two origins. One origin is a dynamic application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. The other origin is an Amazon S3 bucket for static assets. A security analysis shows that HTTPS responses from the application do not comply with a security requirement to provide an X Frame- Options HTTP header to prevent frame-related cross-site scripting attacks. A security engineer must make the full stack compliant by adding the missing HTTP header to the responses. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a Lambda@Edge function. Include code to add the X Frame- Options header to the response. Configure the function to run in response to the CloudFront origin response event.
options.B: Create a Lambda@Edge function. Include code to add the X Frame- Options header to the response. Configure the function to run in response to the CloudFront viewer request event.
options.C: Update the CloudFront distribution by adding X Frame-Options to custom headers in the origin settings.
options.D: Customize the EC2 hosted application to add the X Frame-Options header to the responses that are returned to CloudFront.

explanations.A: Correct. A Lambda@Edge function triggered on the CloudFront origin response event runs after content is returned from either origin and can add the X-Frame-Options header to the response. Because it runs for both the dynamic EC2 origin and the static S3 origin, it makes the full stack compliant.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The CloudFront viewer request event fires when the client request arrives at CloudFront, before any response exists. A function on this event cannot modify HTTP response headers, so it cannot add the X-Frame-Options header.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Custom headers configured in CloudFront origin settings are added to requests that CloudFront sends to the origin; they are not added to the responses returned to the viewer. This would not add the X-Frame-Options header to responses.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Modifying the EC2-hosted application would add the header only to responses from the dynamic origin. Responses served from the S3 static-asset origin would still lack the X-Frame-Options header, so the full stack would not be compliant.

question: An application has been built with Amazon EC2 instances that retrieve messages from Amazon SQS. Recently, IAM changes were made and the instances can no longer retrieve messages. What actions should be taken to troubleshoot the issue while maintaining least privilege? Choose two.)

options.A: Configure and assign an MFA device to the role used by the instances.
options.B: Verify that the SQS resource policy does not explicitly deny access to the role used by the instances.
options.C: Verify that the access key attached to the role used by the instances is active.
options.D: Attach the AmazonSQSFullAccess managed policy to the role used by the instances.
options.E: Verify that the role attached to the instances contains policies that allow access to the queue.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assigning an MFA device is used for user authentication and is not applicable to an IAM role assumed by EC2 instances. It would not resolve the loss of access to Amazon SQS.
explanations.B: Correct. If the SQS resource (queue) policy contains an explicit deny for the role used by the instances, access is blocked even when the IAM role grants the necessary permissions. Verifying that the resource policy does not explicitly deny the role is a valid, least-privilege troubleshooting step.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IAM roles do not authenticate with long-term access keys. EC2 instances obtain temporary credentials automatically through the instance profile, so checking whether an access key is active is not relevant.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Attaching the AmazonSQSFullAccess managed policy could restore access, but it grants far more permission than needed and violates least privilege. The role should be granted only the specific permissions required for the queue.
explanations.E: Correct. If the IAM role attached to the instances lacks a policy that allows the required SQS actions on the queue, the instances cannot retrieve messages. Verifying that the role contains policies allowing access to the queue is a key least-privilege troubleshooting step.

question: A company has an AWS Key Management Service AWS KMS) customer managed key with imported key material. Company policy requires all encryption keys to be rotated every year. What should a security engineer do to meet this requirement for this customer managed key?

options.A: Enable automatic key rotation annually for the existing customer managed key.
options.B: Use the AWS CLI to create an AWS Lambda function to rotate the existing customer managed key annually.
options.C: Import new key material to the existing customer managed key. Manually rotate the key.
options.D: Create a new customer managed key. Import new key material to the new key. Point the key alias to the new key.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Automatic key rotation in AWS KMS is only available for keys where AWS KMS generated the key material. It is not supported for a customer managed key that uses imported key material.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Although a custom Lambda function could be scripted to perform rotation, this is not the AWS-recommended approach for a key with imported key material and adds unnecessary operational complexity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. AWS KMS does not allow you to replace the imported key material of an existing customer managed key with new material to achieve rotation. Rotating imported material requires creating a new key.
explanations.D: Correct. To rotate a customer managed key with imported key material, you create a new customer managed key, import new key material into it, and point the key alias to the new key. This is the AWS-recommended way to rotate keys with imported material.

question: A healthcare company has multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company uses Amazon S3 buckets to store sensitive information of patients. The company needs to restrict users from deleting any S3 bucket across the organization. What is the MOST scalable solution that meets these requirements?

options.A: Permissions boundaries in AWS Identity and Access Management IAM
options.B: S3 bucket policies
options.C: Tag policies
options.D: SCPs

explanations.A: Incorrect. IAM permissions boundaries limit the maximum permissions of individual IAM users or roles within a single account. They cannot enforce an organization-wide restriction across all member accounts, so they do not scale for this requirement.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An S3 bucket policy applies only to the single bucket it is attached to. It cannot centrally prevent bucket deletion across every account in the organization, so it does not provide the required scalability.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tag policies enforce consistent tagging of resources across the organization; they cannot restrict actions such as deleting an S3 bucket. This does not meet the requirement.
explanations.D: Correct. A service control policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations can deny the s3:DeleteBucket action for all member accounts across the organization from a central place. This is the most scalable way to prevent users from deleting any S3 bucket.

question: A company needs to detect unauthenticated access to its Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service Amazon EKS) clusters. Thecompany needs a solution that requires no additional configuration of the existing EKS deployment. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Install an Amazon EKS add-on from a security vendor.
options.B: Enable AWS Security Hub. Monitor the Kubernetes findings.
options.C: Monitor Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights metrics for Amazon EKS.
options.D: Enable Amazon GuardDuty. Use EKS Audit Log Monitoring.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Installing a third-party EKS add-on from a security vendor requires additional configuration and ongoing management, which increases operational effort and does not meet the requirement of no additional configuration to the existing EKS deployment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. AWS Security Hub aggregates and manages security findings but does not itself detect unauthenticated access to EKS clusters. It relies on a data source such as Amazon GuardDuty to produce those Kubernetes findings.
explanations.C: Incorrect. CloudWatch Container Insights collects performance and operational metrics for containers; it is not designed to detect unauthenticated access to the EKS clusters, so it does not meet the security requirement.
explanations.D: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty with EKS Audit Log Monitoring analyzes Kubernetes audit logs to detect unauthenticated and other suspicious access. It requires no additional configuration of the existing EKS deployment, meeting the requirement with the least operational effort.
